sample_unit: LLMs evaluated across three clinical benchmarks

links.outcome: Accuracy and abstention of LLMs in multi-turn conversations versus static clinical benchmarks
links.effect: Partitioning the answer space into sequential presentations reduced end-to-end accuracy and abstention against incorrect suggestions by an average of up to 30%, reaching 65% in certain models.
links.quote: Together our findings demonstrate that the general proficiency captured by static benchmarks do not translate over multi-turn dialogues.

links.outcome: Whether static benchmark performance carries over to multi-turn conversational use
links.effect: Pervasive 'conversation tax' of up to 30% average (65% in some models) and blind switching from abstention to incorrect and correct suggestions at near-identical rates reaching 50%.
links.quote: Together our findings demonstrate that the general proficiency captured by static benchmarks do not translate over multi-turn dialogues.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study evaluating multi-turn conversational robustness, conviction, and abstention across clinical benchmarks for 17 LLMs, but does not test an organizational deployment guardrail or practice.
